title.narrative: Girls' Education and Women's Empowerment and Livelihood Project

description.narrative: The Girl's Education and Women's Empowerment and Livelihoods Project for the Republic of Zambia will support the Government of Zambia to increase access to livelihood support for women and access to secondary education for disadvantaged adolescent girls in extremely poor households in selected districts. The main beneficiaries of the proposed project will be women aged 19 to 64 years old who are fit for work and adolescent girls aged 14 to 18 years old living in extremely poor households in rural areas. The project consists of three components: component 1, supporting women's livelihoods; component 2, keeping girls in school; and component 3, institutional strengthening and systems building. The first component supports women's livelihoods, the second component supports the Keeping Girls in School Initiative, and the third component supports institutional strengthening and system building. The proposed project will not only improve livelihoods and expand access to education through Components 1 and 2 but also aims to improve targeting by building and strengthening systems for implementation. The creation of these systems under this project is expected to further increase the interest of the Government (and external financiers) in investing in livelihood interventions and in covering secondary school fees by channeling funds through the systems that will be set up through this project. Components 1 and 2 will both target extremely poor households, but the categorical targeting used in each component will differ to avoid the same households benefitting from both interventions. Component 1 will target women in households that are not SCTS beneficiaries but are extremely poor and have available labor. Component 2 will target adolescent girls aged 14 to 18 years old in extremely poor households that have high labor dependency ratios and in which the household head is unfit for work. Eligibility for Component 2 will be linked to household enrollment in the SCTS since they represent the most vulnerable households in Zambia.

The project development objective is to support the Government of Zambia to increase access to livelihood support for women and access to secondary education for disadvantaged adolescent girls in extremely poor households in selected districts, and provide cash transfers for poor and vulnerable households.

title.narrative: Share of SCT expenditure financed by GRZ

comment.narrative: Not achieved, reached 87.5 percent at completion. The GRZ allocated funds to cover 70 percent of SCT expenditures in 2024. Due to financial constraints resulting from debt repayment and multiple national emergency responses, the GRZ released 33 percent of the total disbursements to SCT. This indicator was introduced in AF1.

title.narrative: Share of SCT expenditure financed by GRZ

comment.narrative: The GRZ allocated funds to cover 70 percent of SCT expenditures in 2024. Due to financial constraints resulting from debt repayment and multiple ongoing national emergency responses, the GRZ has released 17 percent of total expenditures to date. The situation is expected to improve in 2025.

title.narrative: Share of beneficiaries progressing to next grade

comment.narrative: Not achieved, reached 61 percent at completion, lower than 80 percent target, achieved 76 percent. However, the project has achieved a much higher rate than the national progression rate which stands at 42 percent. The low progression rate reflects the high failure rate on grade 9 exams resulting in low transition to grade 10. This Indicator was introduced in AF1.

title.narrative: Share of beneficiaries progressing to next grade

comment.narrative: The decline in the current value reflects that previous values were reporting on retention and not progression. It was agreed in the last mission to report on progression moving forward. The low progression rate reflects the high failure rate on grade 9 exams resulting in low transition to grade 10. Note that the national progression rate stands at 42%.
